topics.title: South Africa votes amid pressure over basic services
topics.summary: South Africans are voting in local elections as frustration over water outages, power cuts and municipal services weighs heavily on the governing ANC. The result will be watched as a measure of confidence in local leadership.
topics.discussionPrompt: If your town could fix just one everyday service overnight, would you choose buses, streetlights, water, internet, or something more surprising?

topics.title: Canada joins hockey boycott of Russia
topics.summary: Canada has joined countries declining to play ice hockey against Russia after a sports court lifted a competition ban. The dispute shows how international sport can be pulled into wider questions of conflict and participation.
topics.discussionPrompt: Sports are supposed to bring people together, but rules can get complicated fast. What is one sport you think works best as a friendly, no-pressure community event?

topics.title: Drug researchers look to orbit for new ideas
topics.summary: Pharmaceutical firms are exploring experiments in Earth orbit, where microgravity can change how materials and cells behave. Researchers hope those unusual conditions could help them study and develop future medicines.
topics.discussionPrompt: If you could send one ordinary object to orbit just to see what changes, what would you pick: bread dough, a plant, paint, or something else?

topics.title: French blood-storage facilities hit by cyberattack
topics.summary: French blood banks reported a cyberattack affecting cold-storage systems, with temperatures and defrosting settings pushed unusually high. The incident underlines why everyday infrastructure needs both digital and physical safeguards.
topics.discussionPrompt: Some of the most important systems are the ones we barely notice. Which everyday service would you most want protected from a tech outage?

topics.title: Australia debates stronger oversight for automated decisions
topics.summary: A report warns Australia needs clearer auditing and public records for government use of algorithms and AI. The discussion centres on how to make automated decisions understandable, fair and accountable.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a computer helps make a decision about your life, what would you want explained first: the data, the rule, or how to challenge it?

topics.title: Wildlife advocates call for quieter fireworks
topics.summary: Campaigners are urging the UK government to lower permitted firework noise, arguing that loud displays can distress wildlife. The proposal adds a practical design question to familiar celebrations.
topics.discussionPrompt: Would you trade a little spectacle for a quieter celebration that is easier on animals and neighbours? What would make the alternative still feel festive?

topics.title: UN says climate-adaptation funding has stalled
topics.summary: A UN assessment says finance intended to help lower-income countries adapt to climate impacts has stalled. The gap is keeping attention on practical resilience projects as weather risks become harder to ignore.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a community prepares for tougher weather, what feels most useful to you: cooling spaces, better drainage, shade trees, backup power, or neighbour check-ins?

topics.title: Scientists examine penguin colonies and Antarctic snow
topics.summary: New research is exploring how material from penguin colonies can darken Antarctic snow and affect melting. It is a reminder that small changes in surface colour can matter in icy environments.
topics.discussionPrompt: Tiny details can have big effects. What is a small change at home that noticeably changes the mood or comfort of a whole room?

topics.title: Britain considers broader facial-recognition trials
topics.summary: The UK Home Office is preparing possible facial-recognition use at transport hubs and public events for immigration enforcement. The plans are prompting debate over oversight, privacy and how such technology should be governed.
topics.discussionPrompt: Where do you draw the line between convenience and privacy? Would you accept a faster airport queue if it meant more cameras?

topics.title: Markets reassess data-centre and AI expectations
topics.summary: Global markets are reassessing how election results and possible regulation could affect data centres, artificial intelligence and technology companies. Investors are weighing policy uncertainty alongside continuing enthusiasm for new computing infrastructure.
topics.discussionPrompt: Data centres are invisible until one is proposed nearby. What would matter most to you: jobs, electricity use, water, noise, or local control?
